context: A police officer briefs a reporter on community programs
purpose: Teach: 無償/基調/結ば/保っ/欠ける/とらえる/所見/判っ

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 無償の防犯講習、基調はわかりやすさです。
lines.en: These free crime-prevention seminars are built on one principle: clarity.
lines.style: Measured opening. Professional but not stiff. A slight pause before the colon—letting the principle land separately. Steady eye contact, shoulders level. The voice of someone who knows what he's saying matters to people's safety.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 住民と警察が結ばれた事例、印象的です。
lines.en: The cases where residents and police actually connected—those stuck with me.
lines.style: Leaning in slightly, genuinely engaged. Softer than before. A small hesitation on 「connected」—searching for the right word because it matters. Wanting to understand, not just collect information.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: はい。一定の質を保って、欠ける部分は丁寧に補強します。
lines.en: Yes. We keep the standard high, and we shore up whatever's missing with care.
lines.style: Returning to professional register but warmer now. No rush. Each phrase gets its own breath. On 「shore up」 a hint of deliberate gentleness—this isn't bureaucracy, it's careful work.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 被害実態をとらえる視点、深まっています。
lines.en: The way you see victim impact—it's gotten more nuanced.
lines.style: Quiet recognition. Not flattery, observation. A slight tilt forward, genuine. Pause after the dash. The tone of someone acknowledging that another person has grown in their thinking. Respectful.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 所見が判った段階で、行動に移します。
lines.en: Once I understand what you're seeing, we move forward.
lines.style: Quieter, more intimate close. A subtle shift to resolve—not abrupt, but decided. The exhale of someone who trusts the conversation has been real. Shoulders settle. Final word lands with quiet weight.
